154	## Passing a Flow Input Into the Subflow
155	
156	A **parent flow** forwarding its own trigger input into a subflow must give the parent's `in`
157	variable a `triggerNodeId` — same as a subflow `in` variable (rule #3), pointing at the
158	parent's trigger node. Omit it and it's a silent trap: `uip maestro flow validate` still
159	reports **Valid**, but at `flow debug` the trigger output is empty, the value arrives `null`,
160	and the subflow script faults (e.g. `Cannot read property 'split' of null`).
161	
162	**Parent flow `variables.globals`** — note `triggerNodeId` on the `in` variable:
163	```json
164	{
165	  "variables": {
166	    "globals": [
167	      { "id": "text", "direction": "in", "type": "string", "defaultValue": "", "triggerNodeId": "start" },
168	      { "id": "reversedText", "direction": "out", "type": "string", "defaultValue": "" }
169	    ]
170	  }
171	}
172	```
173	
174	**Parent trigger + subflow node** — the subflow node reads the trigger output and maps it to
175	the subflow's `in` variable:
176	```json
177	{
178	  "nodes": [
179	    {
180	      "id": "start",
181	      "type": "core.trigger.manual",
182	      "typeVersion": "1.0",
183	      "inputs": { "entryPointId": "<uuid>", "isDefaultEntryPoint": true },
184	      "outputs": { "output": { "type": "object", "description": "Data passed when manually triggering the process.", "source": "null", "var": "output" } }
185	    },
186	    {
187	      "id": "reverseSubflow",
188	      "type": "core.subflow",
189	      "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
190	      "inputs": { "text": "=js:$vars.start.output.text" }
191	    }
192	  ]
193	}
194	```
195	
196	Value flow: caller input `text` → (bound to `start` via the parent global's `triggerNodeId`)
197	→ `$vars.start.output.text` → subflow node input `text` → the subflow's own `in` variable
198	(with its **own** `triggerNodeId: "<subflowStart>"`) → `$vars.<subflowStart>.output.text`
199	inside the subflow. The parent `in` var and the subflow `in` var are **independent variables
200	in separate scopes**, joined only by the subflow node's `inputs` mapping; each needs its own
201	`triggerNodeId` pointing at its respective Start node.
202	
203	## Subflow Rules
204	
205	1. Every subflow **must** have its own Start node (`core.trigger.manual`) and End node (`core.control.end`)
206	2. Subflow `variables.globals` with `direction: "in"` map to the parent node's `inputs`
207	3. Subflow `in` variables **must** have `triggerNodeId` set to the subflow's Start node ID — this makes them accessible via `$vars.{startNodeId}.output.{varId}`
208	4. Subflow `variables.globals` with `direction: "out"` map to the parent node's outputs, accessible via `$vars.{subflowNodeId}.output` in the parent flow
209	5. Parent-scope `$vars` are **not** visible inside the subflow — pass values explicitly via inputs
210	6. Subflow nodes must have inline `outputs` defined on them (Start node needs `outputs.output`, Script nodes need `outputs.output` and `outputs.error`)
211	7. Subflows can be nested (subflow inside subflow), up to 3 levels
212	8. Each subflow has its own `nodes`, `edges`, `variables`, and `layout` sections
213	9. Subflow node positions go in the subflow's own `layout.nodes` — NOT in the top-level `layout.nodes`. Each subflow scope is independent.
214	10. Parent flow forwarding an external input to a subflow: the parent's `in` variable **must** also set `triggerNodeId` to the parent's trigger node ID — same as #3, one scope up. `uip maestro flow validate` still reports **Valid** (it does not fail on the omission); the value silently arrives `null` at runtime. See [Passing a Flow Input Into the Subflow](#passing-a-flow-input-into-the-subflow).
215	
216	## Creating a Subflow
217	
218	For the step-by-step procedure, see [Edit/Write: Create a subflow](../../editing-operations-json.md#create-a-subflow). Use the parent node JSON and subflow definition structures above for the node-specific fields.

220	## Debug
221	
222	| Error | Cause | Fix |
223	| --- | --- | --- |
224	| `$vars.inputData` undefined inside subflow script | Missing `triggerNodeId` on subflow `in` variable, or using `$vars.{varId}` directly | Add `triggerNodeId: "{startNodeId}"` to each `in` variable and access via `$vars.{startNodeId}.output.{varId}` |
225	| Subflow script sees `null` for a value forwarded from the parent (e.g. `Cannot read property 'split' of null`) | Parent flow's `in` variable is missing `triggerNodeId`, so the parent trigger output is empty and `null` is forwarded into the subflow | Add `triggerNodeId: "{parentStartNodeId}"` to the parent flow's `in` variable (same fix as the row above, but for the root flow) |
226	| `$vars.parentNode` undefined inside subflow | Parent scope not accessible | Pass values via subflow `in` variables |
227	| Subflow output is null | Missing output mapping on subflow's End node | Map all `out` variables in the End node's `outputs` |
228	| Script output is null | Missing inline `outputs` on script node | Add `outputs.output` and `outputs.error` inline on the script node |
229	| Missing Start/End node | Subflow lacks required trigger or end | Add `core.trigger.manual` (with `outputs` and `entryPointId`) and `core.control.end` to the subflow |
230	| Nesting limit exceeded | Subflow nested more than 3 levels deep | Flatten the structure or use resource nodes for deeper composition |

320	
321	Workflow output variables (`direction: "out"`) must be mapped on End nodes. The End node's `outputs` object maps each output variable ID to a source expression.

335	    },

347	## Expression System
348	
349	Flow uses a **Jint-based JavaScript engine** (ES2020 subset) for expressions. There are two expression formats.
350	
351	### `=js:` Expressions (Full JavaScript)
352	
353	Used for conditions, input values, variable updates, and output mappings. The `=js:` prefix tells the engine to evaluate the rest as JavaScript.
354	
355	```
356	=js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.status === "approved"
357	```
358	
359	### Template Expressions (`{ }`)
360	
361	Used for string interpolation in **native flow string fields** only. Expressions inside single braces are evaluated and converted to strings.
362	
363	```
364	Order {$vars.orderId} is {$vars.status} — total: {$vars.amount}
365	```
366	
367	> **Brace-templates do NOT work in Integration Service activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner only processes native flow fields (decision expressions, variable updates, end-node output `source`, script bodies, agent prompt text). Fields inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on `core.action.http.v2` or `uipath.connector.*` activity nodes — `url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` — are passed through to the IS runtime unchanged, so `{$vars.article}` ships literally. Observed behavior: the `$` is stripped and the braces survive (`user/{vars.article}` reaches the service). **For any dynamic value in an IS activity input, use `=js:` instead** — e.g., `` "url": "=js:`https://.../user/${$vars.article}`" `` or `"headers": { "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.token" }`.
368	
369	### IS Activity Inputs Require `=js:` (Critical)
370	
371	Every `$vars` / `$metadata` / `$self` reference inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters`, `inputs.detail.queryParameters`, or `inputs.detail.pathParameters` on a connector or HTTP activity node MUST be wrapped with `=js:`. Without it the value ships as a literal string at runtime.
372	
373	| Wrong | Right |
374	|---|---|
375	| `"recordId": "$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` |
376	| `"recordId": "nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` |
377	| `"recordId": "{vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id}"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` |
378	| `"recordId": "=js:createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` |
379	
380	The serializer rewrites `$vars` → `vars` whether or not `=js:` is present, so a missing prefix yields a confusing failure: the runtime field is bound to the literal string `"vars.X.output.Id"` (which looks like an unevaluated expression). The last row above is the opposite mistake — `=js:` is present but the `$vars.` prefix on the node reference is missing, so the expression evaluates a bare (undefined) identifier instead of the node's output. `flow validate` catches this (cli-side `expression-prefix-validator`, error with remediation hint) — older cli versions without the validator still let it through to `flow debug`. See [node-output-wiring.md](node-output-wiring.md) for the full per-node-type field reference (MST-9107).
381	
382	### Comparison
383	
384	| Feature | `=js:` | `{ }` template |
385	| --- | --- | --- |
386	| Return type | Any (boolean, number, object, array) | Always string |
387	| Use case | Conditions, inputs, mappings | Native flow text/prompt fields only |
388	| Works in IS activity inputs (HTTP URL/headers/body, connector `bodyParameters`) | Yes | **No — use `=js:`** |
389	| Full JS | Yes | Expression-only (no statements) |
390	| Prefix | `=js:` required | No prefix, braces inline |

434	## Expression Contexts
435	
436	Expressions behave differently depending on where they appear.
437	
438	### Script Node Body
439	
440	The `inputs.script` field contains a function body. Full JavaScript statements are allowed (variables, loops, conditionals). The returned value becomes `$vars.{nodeId}.output`.
441	
442	Scripts can return any value — objects, numbers, strings, arrays, or booleans:
443	
444	```javascript
445	// Returning an object (multiple fields)
446	const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items;
447	const filtered = items.filter(i => i.active);
448	return { count: filtered.length, names: filtered.map(i => i.name) };
449	
450	// Returning a bare value (useful for accumulators in loops)
451	return $vars.total + $vars.loop1.currentItem;
452	```
453	
454	### Decision Node (`inputs.expression`)
455	
456	A single boolean expression. Result is coerced to `Boolean()`.
457	
458	```
459	=js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.verified === true
460	```
461	
462	Determines which port fires: `true` or `false`.
463	
464	### Switch Node (`inputs.cases[].expression`)
465	
466	Each case has an expression evaluated in order. First truthy result wins; otherwise the `default` port fires.
467	
468	```json
469	{
470	  "inputs": {
471	    "cases": [
472	      { "label": "Low", "expression": "$vars.score <= 30" },
473	      { "label": "Medium", "expression": "$vars.score <= 70" },
474	      { "label": "High", "expression": "$vars.score > 70" }
475	    ]
476	  }
477	}
478	```
479	
480	### HTTP Branch Condition (`inputs.branches[].conditionExpression`)
481	
482	Uses `$self` to reference the current HTTP node's response.
483	
484	```
485	$self.output.statusCode >= 200 && $self.output.statusCode < 300
486	```
487	
488	### Variable Update Expressions
489	
490	Evaluate to the new value for the target variable.
491	
492	```
493	=js:$vars.counter + 1
494	=js:$vars.items.concat([$vars.newItem.output])
495	```
496	
497	### Loop Collection Expression
498	
499	The `inputs.collection` field on a Loop node resolves to an array to iterate over.
500	
501	```
502	=js:$vars.fetchData.output.body.items
503	=js:$vars.inputArray.filter(x => x.active)
504	```
505	
506	Inside the loop body, use `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem` and `$vars.<loopId>.currentIndex` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`).

510	## Jint Engine Constraints
511	
512	The production runtime uses **Jint** (a .NET JavaScript interpreter, ES2020 subset). Key constraints:
513	
514	### Supported
515	
516	- Arithmetic: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%`
517	- Comparison: `===`, `!==`, `==`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`
518	- Logical: `&&`, `||`, `!`
519	- Ternary: `condition ? a : b`
520	- String methods: `.toUpperCase()`, `.toLowerCase()`, `.trim()`, `.split()`, `.includes()`, `.startsWith()`, `.slice()`, `.substring()`
521	- Array methods: `.filter()`, `.map()`, `.reduce()`, `.find()`, `.some()`, `.every()`, `.concat()`, `.length`
522	- Object: `Object.keys()`, `Object.values()`, `Object.entries()`
523	- Math: `Math.floor()`, `Math.ceil()`, `Math.round()`, `Math.abs()`, `Math.min()`, `Math.max()`, `Math.random()`
524	- JSON: `JSON.parse()`, `JSON.stringify()`
525	- Template literals: `` `Hello ${name}` ``
526	- Destructuring: `const { a, b } = obj` (in script bodies)
527	- Spread operator: `[...arr1, ...arr2]` (in script bodies)
528	- Arrow functions: `items.filter(x => x.active)` (inline callbacks)
529	
530	### Not Supported
531	
532	- `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval` — no network or timers
533	- `document`, `window`, `console` — no DOM or browser globals
534	- `require`, `import` — no module system
535	- `eval`, `Function` constructor — no dynamic code generation
536	- `async`/`await`, `Promise` — no async operations
537	- `Date` constructor may have limited support — prefer ISO 8601 strings
538	
539	> **When in doubt, keep expressions simple.** Complex data processing should go in Script nodes where you have full statement support, not in one-line expressions.
540	
541	**Script:** `python3 scripts/lint_jint.py <flow>` scans every `core.action.script` body and every `=js:` expression for the unsupported constructs listed above, plus the script-node rules (top-level `return` of an object, no `function main()` wrapper, no `console.log`, no `aggregate` variable). None of these are caught by `uip maestro flow validate`.

545	## Scoping Rules
546	
547	### Node Output Availability
548	
549	A node's output (`$vars.{nodeId}.output`) is available to **all downstream nodes** connected via edges. If a node has not executed (e.g., on an untaken branch), its `$vars` entry is `undefined`.
550	
551	### Loop Scope
552	
553	Inside a loop body, you have access to:
554	- All parent-scope `$vars` (read-only from loop's perspective)
555	- `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem` — current array element
556	- `$vars.<loopId>.currentIndex` — zero-based index
557	- `$vars.<loopId>.collection` — the original array
558	
559	Where `<loopId>` is the loop node's `id` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`).
560	
561	> **Important:** Loop body nodes must have `"parentId": "<loopId>"` set in their JSON. Without this, the runtime does not know the node is inside the loop and `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem` will be undefined.
562	
563	After loop completion, `$vars.<loopId>.output` contains aggregated results from all iterations.
564	
565	### Subflow Scope
566	
567	Subflows have their own variable scope. Parent variables are **not** automatically visible inside a subflow. Pass values explicitly via subflow `inputs` and receive results via subflow `outputs`.
568
